comments.content: The `doneCount` calculation duplicates the `tasks.filter(...)` logic already present in the `rfNodes` useMemo (line 592-594) for the goal card progress. Both compute the same value from the same data. Consider extracting a single source of truth (e.g., a shared `useMemo`) so the two call sites stay in sync and the duplication is removed.

The new `title` branch overrides `runButtonTitle(dirty, …)` whenever `doneCount > 0`, which loses the "先保存再执行" hint that the helper surfaces when `dirty` is true. Result: with unsaved changes (`dirty`) AND completed nodes, the button is disabled but its title still reads "继续执行：已完成 X 个节点将跳过…" — misleading because the actual blocker is the dirty state, not anything related to resumption. Recommend gating the "继续执行" title on `doneCount > 0 && !dirty` (or composing both hints), so the dirty-state warning still wins when applicable.

Fuse detection relies on `text.contains("已熔断")`, creating an undocumented string-coupling with `bot_model_loop.rs:337` (the `fuse_message` formatter). If the wording there is ever rephrased, i18n-ed, or the emoji `⏹` removed, the workflow controller silently degrades — no ⚠️ note written, but the `ok` flag is still computed from the DB so failure propagation still happens. The user just loses the actionable 「调高上限后重跑」 hint. Consider surfacing fuse as a structured signal (e.g. extend `BotChatResult` with `fused: bool` set inside `bot_model_loop.rs` next to the fuse return) so this contract is type-checked, not string-matched.

Also worth noting: the same brittle coupling now exists in two places (`workflow_runner.rs` here + `bot_scheduler.rs` ⏰ 摘要), so a structured field would fix both.

comments.content: `NodeOutcome` now carries three independent booleans (`ok` / `cancelled` / `fused`) whose valid combinations are implicit (e.g. `ok=true, cancelled=true` or `ok=true, fused=true` are representable but meaningless). With fuse added, the cross-product grows again. Consider collapsing to a single `enum Outcome { Ok, Failed, FailedFused, Cancelled }` — `cancelled` already short-circuits at the consumer (line 382) so the fused/failed pair is the only one the receiver needs to distinguish. A typed variant also removes the duplicated `fused: false` writes on the cancellation path.

Per-keystroke saveConfig will trigger bot_set_config IPC + disk write on every character typed. The pythonTimeoutSecs pattern (lines 1815-1821) only updates local state and saves on explicit save. Consider the same approach: hold value in local state, debounce or save onBlur, to avoid disk thrash when typing multi-digit values.

The onChange handler in the input directly calls saveConfig which means typing "100" = 3 sequential disk writes (well, debounced by configBusy lock, but still sub-optimal vs local state pattern).

comments.content: The label "(全域熔断)" and help text emphasize "全局/所有机器人执行（含普通聊天）", but the input lives inside the WorkflowSettingsCard which only renders when activeSection === "workflow". Users who don't open the workflow section will never see this global setting. The spec explicitly puts it in the workflow section, but consider whether a non-workflow user can ever discover/disable this cap if they hit it in regular chat. Worth confirming intent with PM, or adding a brief hint on the chat side when the cap fires (already handled in the W5-FUSE spec via the note prefix).

comments.content: Dead code: `let mut calls = 0usize;` is declared but never used after this line — the closure `(1..=31).any(|n| should_fuse(n, 30))` does not reference `calls`. Remove this line to keep the test clean (clippy `unused_variables` / `dead_code`).

Construction of `fuse_cap_override` always wraps a `Some(...)`, making the downstream `.unwrap_or(MAX_FUNCTION_CALLS_PER_REQUEST)` dead code in production (only reachable from tests passing `None`). Consider simplifying to `fuse_cap_override: cfg.max_function_calls.map(|v| v.max(1) as usize)` so the fallback to the default lives in exactly one place (the chain in `run_model_loop_core`).

Per-keystroke saveConfig triggers bot_set_config IPC + disk write on every character typed. The pythonTimeoutSecs input (line 1815-1821) follows the local-state pattern — only updates setConfig and saves on explicit save. Consider mirroring that pattern here: hold the value in local state, then either debounce the save or save onBlur, to avoid disk thrash when typing multi-digit values. The configBusy lock (line 704) prevents concurrent writes but each keystroke still queues an IPC round-trip.

comments.content: The new title ternary partially bypasses the `runButtonTitle()` helper that OCR r1 extracted specifically to avoid inline conditional logic in `title`. Extend `runButtonTitle` to accept `doneCount` (or add a sibling helper) so all tooltip variants live in one named place — e.g. `runButtonTitle(dirty, hasActive, doneCount)` — instead of splitting the logic across the inline expression and the helper.

Parallel to the already-confirmed `dirty` issue: when `nodes.length === 0` but `doneCount > 0` (e.g. all nodes were deleted but done tasks remain), the button is disabled yet the title still reads "继续执行：已完成 X 个节点将跳过…" — misleading. The override currently ignores all disabled reasons; the `runButtonTitle`/`dirty` branch handles `dirty` correctly, but `nodes.length === 0` slips through. Fold the nodes-length check (and ideally all disabled reasons) into the central helper.

Test name `fuse_trips_on_51st_function_call` is stale after W5-FUSE: the test body now exercises 101 calls (matching the new default 100 cap) and the internal panic message says "101 次 Function 调用内必须触发熔断". Rename to `fuse_trips_on_101st_function_call` so the name accurately describes behavior.

Stale comment: "MAX_FUNCTION_CALLS_PER_REQUEST = 50 实际生效" no longer matches the constant value (now 100). The two lines directly above have already been updated to reflect 50→100; this intro line should be too.

comments.content: Boundary assertion still uses cap=50 (the old default), not the new default cap=100. With the default raised to 100, the boundary case should also be exercised at the new default to lock in the changed contract: `!should_fuse(100, 100)` and `should_fuse(101, 100)`. The existing cap=50 pair remains useful as an explicit boundary-semantics check, but should be clearly labeled as such (not "边界" implying default behavior).

Input has no upper bound (no `max` attr, no JS clamp, backend accepts any `u32`). A user could enter `999999999` and effectively disable the global circuit breaker — defeating the W5-FUSE guard. Inconsistent with `pythonTimeoutSecs` whose comment documents a backend hard cap ("硬钳 300s"); here the comment is silent. Suggest either: (1) add a sensible upper bound (frontend `max` + backend clamp) with a brief help-text note, or (2) explicitly state in the help text that there is no enforced cap so users understand the implication.
